key_scheme: Epics are milestones M0 to M10 (plus F0, the summer foundation). Stories are GRD-### and map one-to-one to Jira issues. Statuses: done, active, todo, parked.

milestones.title: Foundation
milestones.plain: The groundwork built over the summer: pull the official play list for a game, model the field in real yards, cut a 96-minute film into its 184 plays, and chat with the data.
milestones.proof: 158 tests pass. The demo game's film was cut into exactly 184 plays, the same count as the official play-by-play.

stories.title: Project scaffold and package layout
NFL field model in yards (landmarks, hashes, LOS anchor)
Play-by-play puller from nflverse with stable play ids
Personnel and formation parser
DuckDB store with enriched play table
Chat brain: two constrained tools over the store
Shot segmentation of continuous film (cut detection, tilt signal)
Hand-labelled camera-angle ground truth for the demo game
Play index: Viterbi view labelling, merge, pair, join to play-by-play
Second play-by-play source client
stories.note: Built 2026-07-26, parked 2026-09-11. The NFL API covers the need.

milestones.title: Research, planning, decisions
milestones.plain: Decide what to build and in what order. Write the blueprint. Pick the tools. Set up this tracker so everyone can follow along.
milestones.proof: Closed 2026-09-13: blueprint, play record contract, correction loop, ingestion and live design, tracker, film room demo, every open decision answered.

milestones.title: Ingestion and the NFL API
milestones.plain: Get the film and the official data into a shape the vision code can eat: a cheaper copy of the video, one clip per play per angle, and a Python client for the NFL's own API.
milestones.proof: Closed 2026-09-13: every play of the demo game exists as a record from official data (NFL API backbone, free labels merged by play id); ingestion, proxy, clips and film-window detection tested on synthetic video; fz-run skips unchanged work. 209 tests.

stories.title: NFL API credentials available on the build machine

stories.title: Probe and proxy: video metadata sidecar and a 540p frame-aligned rendition
stories.note: Done; first real run 2026-09-14: the demo recording probes at 244,505 frames, 25 fps, 163 min in both the 576p and 1080p renditions, so they are frame-aligned. Keyframe every 6.7 s in the source; the proxy puts one every second.

stories.title: Per-play clips for both angles from the play index
stories.note: Done: fz-clips cuts both angles per play with a pad and a manifest mapping clip frame 0 to the source frame.

stories.note: Verified live 2026-09-13: token exchange, weekly slate, game detail (218 rows, 184 filmable = film), rosters (90 and 83 players). Playoff week mapping confirmed (week 20 = POST 2).

stories.note: Done: every free-data play id exists in the NFL payload, so labels merge by exact play id, not position. 184 = 184.

stories.title: Find the film window automatically inside a screen recording (no typed start and end)
stories.note: Done on real film 2026-09-14: motion-and-brightness rule finds the film within 30 s of the hand-found span on the snow game, and in 30 s on the clear game. Colour was abandoned: snow.

stories.title: Frame source interface with file and stream implementations
stories.note: Done: FileSource and StreamSource behind one interface.

milestones.title: Label bootstrap
milestones.plain: Make the training data without drawing boxes by hand. A big slow model labels sampled frames; a human approves contact sheets with one key per image; a small fast model learns from it.
milestones.proof: A detector trained from zero hand-drawn boxes, and the review sheet took under 30 minutes.

stories.title: Camera-angle classifier: contact-sheet review of takes, tiny model on downscaled frames, alternation prior; validate by play count on both games
stories.note: Done 2026-10-30. The labels had the two names swapped (corrected in both games). Per-game model on colour layout plus line direction, read every 0.4 s: 100% / 95% held out on the snow / clear game; neither transfers between games yet, so each game needs ~40 sheet labels. Validated through the play count by GRD-96.

stories.title: Spike-based cut detection: a cut is a spike against its neighbours, not an absolute threshold
stories.note: Done 2026-09-14: a cut is a spike against its neighbours' median (ratio 2.5, floor 8). Clear game: 286 takes vs 282 implied.

stories.title: Take alignment: pair the film's takes to the plays on film (sequence alignment with false cuts, missed cuts, footage outside plays, optional plays)
stories.note: Done 2026-10-30: perception/align.py, the pipeline's dense and play_index stages. Count the rows that put a play on film (nullified snaps yes; pre-snap fouls and kneel-downs optional, chosen by how predictable play types become). Snow game 185 on film / 183 indexed, clear game 147 / 141; all 46 kicks land on their film. The old index had ~55 plays on the wrong film.

stories.title: Take boundaries: audit every boundary with a geometric camera reading and move the misplaced ones
stories.note: Found 2026-10-30 by the field-line work (GRD-37): some boundaries inside the play index are off by seconds, though every play is on its own film. Confirmed by eye on the clear game: p064's end-zone take starts at 2011.6 s, before the snap (index 2014.4, a missed cut beside a false one), and p062's sideline take opens with 4 s of an end-zone shot. Moving boundaries to where the 0.4 s camera reading flips would touch 11 (snow) and 31 (clear) boundaries, but 2 of 3 such moves checked by eye were wrong: the reading errs on unusual shots (wide end-zone, tight sideline), which is where boundaries are. Plan: read the camera from yard-line direction (flat = end zone, steep = sideline; perception/field/lines.py) near each boundary, and split takes at strong full-rate cuts during tracking. First try of the line reading with no angle label, on 16 clear-game frames judged by eye around these boundaries: 11 right; all 5 end-zone frames of p062 and p064 read as sideline (hash-mark columns look like steep yard lines); snow frames too faint to read. Needs a hash-row test before it can audit boundaries. Separately, take ends run late by up to one 0.4 s reading: on 49ers-Rams plays 1-10, 19 of 20 takes ran 3 to 17 frames past their cut. Tracking now trims each take at a full-rate cut near its ends (GRD-34); the index itself is unchanged.

stories.title: Frame sampler stratified by angle, phase, and half of the film
stories.note: Done 2026-10-30: labelling/sample.py (fz-sample). 2,000 frames per game, 166-167 in each angle x phase x half stratum, every play used; phase is a guess from position in the take until snap detection. --extract saves source-resolution JPEGs to the film drive.

stories.title: SAM 3 teacher: text prompts to boxes and masks, geometry filters
stories.note: Snow game done 2026-10-30 (2,000 frames, 3.4 h, 6.1 s a frame); 49ers-Rams running. Checked by eye on 12 random frames: players and referees nearly all boxed, few false boxes; the errors are bench players and staff in wide kickoff shots, the odd box around two players, and people cut by the frame edge. Balls: precise at 0.4 and up (21 of 24 right), about half wrong below, found in one frame in eight; the detections file cuts balls at 0.4. 49ers-Rams relabelled from a 1080p copy (frame for frame with the 576p one) from 2026-10-30 evening; the 576p labels are kept as *.576p.json. The 1080p run (2026-10-30, 5.5 s a frame) against the 576p one on the same frames: players nearly the same (+0.3% end zone, +3.6% sideline, the gain mostly bench players in uniform), balls more than doubled on sideline frames (143 to 306; most of the new ones checked by eye are the ball). In close shots the shield's ball passed the height filter (21 of the 23 balls wider than 2.2:1), so balls more than 2.5 times as wide as tall now go too, reapplied to the log; the snow game's file is unchanged.

stories.title: Review contact sheets: one-key approve / reject / flag, saved as JSON
stories.note: Built 2026-10-30: labelling/review.py (fz-review build / import). Tested in headless Chrome on the snow game's 2,000 frames, which found two bugs, now fixed: no boxes were drawn, and every full-size frame was decoded at once. Boxes are SVG over lazy images; space enlarges a frame, where a click removes one box (D-015 amended). On 49ers-Rams sideline frames, boxes whose feet are off the field start removed (labelling/field_filter.py, never more than half a frame's boxes; a click restores them; snow left out). Both games' pages are built most disputed first, from round 0's held-out disagreement (GRD-31): the top of each is wide kickoff shots with benches, snow pile-ups, and boxes drawn around several players. Pages: <film root>/<season>/<week>/<game>/frames/review.html. Waits on the owner's review. 49ers-Rams page rebuilt from the 1080p labels 2026-10-30 (tested in headless Chrome: loads, most disputed first, no errors); 3,720 bench boxes on 583 frames start removed. The 576p page stays in frames_576p. 2026-10-31: pre-removals judged in yards on sideline frames that register (field_filter.feet_off), done for the first 600 frames of the 49ers-Rams page: frames left with 20-24 player boxes 239 to 364, over 26 from 203 to 72; six random frames by eye removed only sideline people. Picture guide on the drive (review_guide.html). A review round is about 300 frames a game: labelling.train picks the next round's frames. First approved labels 2026-10-31: 371 frames kept across both games. Of 2,724 pre-removals on 49ers-Rams 35 were restored (33 officials, 2 players). Yards pre-removal fails on the snow game (52 of 85 suggestions were boxes the owner kept), so snow stays hand-reviewed.

stories.title: Train the first student detector; disagreement-driven second round
stories.note: Code 2026-10-30: labelling/train.py (fz-train export / fit / disagree / heldout): YOLO dataset split by play, YOLO11-s fine-tune, and the next review sheet from teacher-student disagreements. The student learns players and referees, not the ball (the teacher finds it in one frame in eight). Round 0 done 2026-10-30 on the unreviewed teacher boxes of both games, two folds by play, each trained on half the plays and scoring the other half: 960 px, batch 4, 8 epochs, validation only at the end (1280 px at batch 8 swapped the 16 GB laptop to a standstill), 1.3 and 1.6 h a fold. Against the teacher on its held-out plays: mAP50 0.94, players recall 0.90-0.91 at precision 0.95-0.97, referees about 0.80 / 0.85. Held-out disagreement averages 3.2 boxes a frame on the snow game and 5.5 on 49ers-Rams (576p); it orders the review pages. Round 1 waits on the review. On 49ers-Rams' 1080p labels the same students disagree on 6.3 boxes a frame (5.5 at 576p): they learned from the 576p labels, and the 1080p teacher boxes more of the benches. Round 1 (2026-10-31): 371 approved frames, continuing from round 0. Held-out player mAP50 0.837 to 0.958, referee 0.677 to 0.871, flattered because round 0's disputes chose those frames; player recall did not rise. On random 49ers-Rams sideline frames bench 'players' fell from 4.2 a frame to 0.1, referees on the field held; the snow game did not move. NMS IoU 0.5 clears most stacked boxes on linemen with no labelling. Half the plays against all: player mAP50 0.950 to 0.956, referee 0.850 to 0.871, so close to flat for players in these two games. A third game is unmeasured. Final student on all 371 frames in runs/student; next sheets built (300 frames a game) but not yet on the review page. In tracking, round 1 helps the geometry but finds about 0.6 fewer players a frame before the snap (real linemen in the clump), so 40 random frames of Chargers-Chiefs, a game neither model trained on, were reviewed as a test. Result, 38 frames, 711 players: player precision 0.798 to 0.952, recall 0.959 to 0.951 (change within noise), referee precision 0.587 to 0.889. Tracking moves to the round-1 student at NMS 0.5. fz-train test repeats the score for any model; 8 of the 34 false boxes left are the painted NFL shield.

stories.title: Measure SAM 3 throughput on the M4 (the number the whole plan assumes)
stories.note: Done 2026-10-30: scripts/spikes/sam3_throughput. Runs on MPS with four in-process shims. 0.29 fps rested, 0.16 settled (fanless), so ~236 h per game and ~3.5 h for 2,000 labelling frames; 1080p and 576p cost the same (1008x1008 inside). Players and referees usable; football judged unusable here, revised by the full run (GRD-29): precise at 0.4 and up, low recall.

milestones.title: Detect, track, team split
milestones.plain: On every frame of every clip, find the players and the ball, follow each one over time, and sort them into home, away, and officials.
milestones.proof: An overlay video of ten plays with stable player ids and correct team colours.

stories.title: Detector behind a protocol; YOLO11 and RF-DETR implementations
stories.note: Started 2026-10-30: perception/base.py (Detections, Detector, Tracker, TeamClassifier protocols) and perception/detect/yolo.py. The COCO stand-in is weak: on 60 snow-game frames yolo11s finds 80% of the teacher's players (75% sideline) and adds 5 to 9 other people a frame; the student replaces it. RF-DETR not started.

stories.title: ByteTrack tracking with per-track confidence and fragmentation
stories.note: Started 2026-10-30: perception/track/bytetrack.py, one supervision ByteTrack per label (supervision dropped ByteTrack in 0.30, pinned below), and a per-track summary (coverage, gaps, confidence) with a per-take fragment count; perception/tracking.py runs both takes of chosen plays straight from the source film. Smoke-tested on 50 frames. First real run 2026-10-30: 49ers-Rams plays 1-10 with a round-0 student at 960 px, 20 to 33 frames a second on the laptop. Settings measured on five takes (bytetrack.py docstring): low-score boxes kept for ByteTrack's second match, matching at IoU 0.1, players and referees in one tracker with a per-track label vote; BoT-SORT's camera-motion compensation did no better. Each take is cut-checked at full rate: index spans ran 3 to 17 frames into the next shot on 19 of 20 takes, now trimmed, and a cut or freeze-jump inside ends every track. Fragments per take went from 48-129 to 3-45, except two end-zone takes where the film freezes and jumps or the camera zooms out in four frames (70 and 93). Play 10 by eye: ids hold through the snap and most of the run on both angles. Bench players and staff are tracked as players; the field mask is next. Player tracks whose feet stay off the field are marked off_field on sideline takes and drawn grey (vote_field): of 165, nearly all were benches, staff, chain crew and cheerleaders; it misses benches when their sideline paint is out of shot or within the mask's margin. Retracked from the 1080p copy 2026-10-30: the same spans and cuts on all 20 takes, the same on-field player boxes per frame, tracks 1,544 to 1,621 and fragments 474 to 495, about 20 frames a second. No gain yet, as expected: the detector sees every frame at 960 px either way, and the student learned from 576p labels. From 2026-10-30 night the off-field vote judges feet in yards where the frame registers (GRD-37), the mask only elsewhere: the mask's far boundary often sat on the team area and its near one 3 yd inside the field. Plays 1-10: 256 sideline tracks off against 152; the 118 added are benches and sideline staff (116 seen by eye), 14 dropped within 1.4 yd of the near sideline.

stories.title: Team classifier (SigLIP embeddings), reconciled across the game
stories.note: Colour path first, 2026-10-30 (a background agent; SigLIP not started): perception/team.py, shirt and pants colour histograms with the crop's own field colour down-weighted (works on snow), 2-means refined by LDA, team 0 the lighter shirts. Agent's count on random crops: 64/65 and 72/73 snow by half, 90/90 clear; Claude's recount of the hardest sheet and of three whole snow frames puts single crops nearer 90-95%, errors mostly small, blurred Rams on the snow at low margins. Tracks vote with the median of confident margins (tracking.py), fitted once per game on the teacher's crops. On play 10 of 49ers-Rams (12 frames by eye) the colours were right: 49ers yellow, Rams cyan. Id swaps 2026-10-31 (tracking.swap_cuts): opposing linemen locked together swap track ids, so one track carried a 49er and then a Ram and took one team for both. A track is now cut where its colour changes for good, the rest under a new id: 427 of 2,904 on-field sideline tracks on plays 1-60, 29 of 30 random cuts real swaps by eye. Players on the wrong side of the line before the snap 25 on 20 takes before, 5 on 4 after. tracking --revote redoes teams without detecting again.

stories.title: Overlay video export
stories.note: Started 2026-10-30: perception/overlay.py draws ids and team (or label) colours and writes an MP4 per take (tracking.py --overlay). Overlays of 49ers-Rams plays 1-10 on the film drive (2026/wk01/SF_at_LA/overlays/pNNN.<angle>.mp4): ids, team colours, officials red. Overlays now from the 1080p copy; the 576p ones moved to overlays_576p.

milestones.title: Field registration and the 2D view
milestones.plain: Turn pixels into yards. Find the yard lines and hashes in each frame, pin them to the known line of scrimmage, and project every player onto a top-down field. This is the milestone that decides whether the whole thing works.
milestones.proof: A bird's-eye video of ten plays, and the formation frame agrees with the official formation label.

stories.title: Classical line detection plus LOS anchor for easy frames
stories.note: Lines and field mask started 2026-10-30 (a background agent, reviewed): perception/field/lines.py, top-hat plus ridge line pixels, Hough, vanishing-point families, boundaries where yard-line paint stops, mask inside them; 0.2 s a frame on CPU. Clear game good: yard lines 30/30 end zone, 25/30 sideline, far sideline 17/22; on kickoff frames the mask drops both benches (16 of 52 people a frame). Snow weak: end zone 9/15 first half, ~1/15 second; no answer on wide snow shots. Of 274 removals checked, 20 were on-field players, all on 3 frames with a false boundary. Hash rows, homography and LOS anchor 2026-10-30 (a background agent, reviewed; perception/field/hashes.py, homography.py): yard lines put on the 5-yd grid, rows of dashes on whole yards, rows named by the camera each naming implies (a wrong naming fits as well but puts the camera under the field or 140+ yd away), RANSAC fit, then on pre-snap frames a whole number of 5-yd steps from where the two lines of players meet against the official yard line. Clear game at 1080p: 654 of 1,001 sideline samples easy (2.3 px median error; after the whistle only 107 of 333, mostly close-ups); the camera 87 yd back and 27 yd up on every easy frame; fitted on the hash rows alone, the far sideline ticks land 0.07 yd from the paint; the players' line 0.19 yd from the official one (median, max 1.02); 69 of 69 anchored frames agree with the painted yard numbers by eye. End zone: relative only (41 of 60 easy), no anchor; snow not tried; yard numbers not read; 0.9 s a frame. It also exposed misplaced take boundaries in the clear game's play index. First use: the tracker's off-field vote (GRD-34). Second use: the bird's-eye view (GRD-39, GRD-43). Second stadium 2026-10-31: Chargers-Chiefs, no model trained on it, plays 61-120 held out: 49 of 55 anchored, median 0.14 yd from the official line, 0.97 at worst, once team colours handled shade (perception/team.py) and each game's camera was measured from its own frames (topdown.game_camera).

stories.title: Self-labelled field keypoints; train and iterate the keypoint model
Per-frame homography with temporal smoothing and rejection
stories.note: First version 2026-10-30 night in perception/field/topdown.py (a background agent, reviewed): the camera's motion between consecutive frames (corners tracked with the players masked out, one homography a frame pair, 12 ms; a fit on all 3,415 pairs of 49ers-Rams plays 1-10) chains registrations every 10th frame into one relative frame and fills the frames between. Scored against direct registrations at the players' feet: 0.035 yd median a frame, 0.45 yd worst (p95), the same for registrations every 2 to 25 frames, which is the registrations' own scatter; blending registrations without the motion gives 3.5 yd worst every 5 frames. The 5-yd step between registrations is never in doubt (at most 0.14 yd from a whole step; player continuity agrees on 245 of 253, the rest in a fast punt pan where ids switch). The motion alone carries 4 s past the last registration (0.08 yd median drift at 3-4 s), so no frame lacks a homography; 15% are carried that way, mostly close-ups after the whistle. Rejection: a registration the motion contradicts from both neighbours is dropped (none were). Held out 2026-10-31 on plays 11-60 (18,627 frames, nothing changed after the run): 2.3% of frames without a homography (167 on one goal-line play), 2 registrations dropped, no step in doubt.

stories.title: Snap detection and pre / live / post phases from line motion
stories.note: First version 2026-10-30 night (topdown.snap_frame): the snap is where the players' median speed in yards leaves a still set for good (over 2 yd/s for 0.4 s, stepped back to the last frame under 0.5). It times the anchor (all 38 frames before each snap give the same shift on 9 of 9 takes) and the line-of-scrimmage check. Phases after the snap not yet. Held out on plays 11-60: a snap on 49 of 50 takes; the one missing is a goal-line play with almost no homographies before it. Third-game gap 2026-10-31: 8 of 110 scrimmage takes saw no snap: 4 of 5 field goals, where almost nobody moves, 2 goal-line runs where the end zone fills the frame and nothing registers, and 2 others.

stories.title: Ball trajectory fit
Two-angle fusion at snap-aligned time
Top-down render, MP4 and contact sheets
stories.note: Started 2026-10-30 night (a background agent, reviewed): perception/field/topdown.py. Bird's-eye positions and videos of 49ers-Rams plays 1-10, sideline takes. Each take gets a positions parquet (absolute yards, team, how the frame's homography was got) and an MP4 on the drive (birdseye/): the broadcast overlay with the absolute yard lines drawn on it, above a to-scale field with team dots, ids, the official line of scrimmage and the camera's footprint. 9 of 10 takes absolute; p001 is a kickoff the take joins after the kick, so there is no line of scrimmage and it stays relative. By eye the drawn yard lines sit on the painted ones on every frame checked, including a wide punt pan and close-ups carried 3-4 s past the last registration. Which club is which team colour comes from the anchor too (summed residual 1.4 yd against 12.2 swapped). At the snap the offense's front three stand 0.1-1.1 yd behind the official line and the defense's 0.4-1.4 beyond on 7 of 9 takes (the other two spoiled by tracker team labels); 22 players on the field on 58% of pre-snap frames, 20-24 on 95%. Near-bench people seen over the heads in front had landed up to 2.9 yd inside the field: boxes are now also judged cut off by the frame's bottom from the head and the camera (homography.feet; 584 boxes). Not yet: end-zone takes; positions are raw box bottoms (3% of speeds over 11 yd/s, from id switches and occlusion); the formation half of the proof (a shotgun-depth rule, set after looking, fits 6 of 6 plays where it decides). 0.10 s a frame on the CPU, plus the video. Held out 2026-10-31 on plays 11-60 of the same game (50 sideline takes, none looked at while building, nothing changed after the run): 45 of 47 scrimmage plays anchored (players' line 0.16 yd from the official one, median; max 0.9); the two left relative are a pass from the 2 with the end zone filling the picture, and a play where four 49ers in the clump at the line carry the Rams' team label, which the anchor's check refuses. By eye the drawn yard lines sit on the painted lines and numbers on one random frame of each of the 46 anchored takes. Fronts in the band on 39 of 46, the misses mostly tracker team labels. The shotgun rule decides on 23 of 42 pass and run plays and agrees with the play-by-play on 21; it leaves 17 under-centre plays undecided. The misses checked by eye are the tracker's team colours on clumped linemen, not the geometry; goal-line plays where the end zone fills the picture still go without a homography. Rerun with the tracker's id-swap cuts (not held out, the rule was set on these plays): p029 anchors and no other take moved; plays 11-60 46 of 47 anchored, fronts on 43 of 47, the formation rule decides 25 of 43 and agrees on 23; plays 1-10 fronts on 9 of 9.

milestones.title: Football intelligence and the play record
milestones.plain: Read football from the positions, phase by phase. Before the snap: the formation, who shifted, who motioned and which way. At the snap: the formation as it stood, who was still moving. Live: every receiver's route, the run gap and scheme, the quarterback's drop, the coverage, the ball's flight. After: the tackle, the spot, the yards. Every player gets a direction and body orientation on every frame. It all lands in one JSON record per play.
milestones.proof: A complete play record for every play of the demo game, validated against the schema, and the chat answers 'show me every jet motion into a Cover 3' from our own vision output.

stories.title: Role assignment from the formation frame (QB, RB, WR, TE, line, EDGE, LB, CB, S)
Defensive line technique (0 to 9, wide-9, head-up) and stance
Pre-snap: initial formation, shifts, motions with type and direction, formation at the snap
Per-player direction and body orientation on every frame; sampled at the snap
Live routes: route-tree label, break frame, depth and direction of break, target
Live run plays: ball carrier, gap, scheme, blocks and engagements
Quarterback: drop type, time to throw, pocket, scramble; ball release and arrival
Defense: coverage family, man or zone, rotation, pass rush paths, blitz
Events timeline and post-snap: first contact, tackle, spot, yards after catch, out of bounds
Play record assembler: fill every section with source and confidence, validate, write JSON
Assembler respects corrections: apply the JSONL log, keep the machine value, never re-run a reviewed play
Validate every module on Big Data Bowl tracking data first

milestones.title: Reasoning router
milestones.plain: When the local models cannot tell what happened (a goal-line pile, a contested catch, a lost ball), send a handful of frames to a hosted vision model and ask. With a budget, a cache, and a record of who answered.
milestones.proof: Goal-line plays resolved with the source recorded, and re-running the game costs nothing.

stories.title: Trigger rules from pipeline quality signals
Async router with budget, concurrency, retries, content-hash cache
Anthropic provider; OpenAI and Gemini behind the same protocol
Keyframe picker with SAM 3 masks
Merge results into labels without overwriting local estimates

milestones.title: Player identity
milestones.plain: Put names on the dots. Read jersey numbers across a track, match to the roster, and cross-check against the NFL API's record of who touched each play.
milestones.proof: Player names in the top-down view, validated against the NFL API's per-play jersey records.

stories.title: Weak jersey labels from contact-sheet reads constrained to the roster
Promote tracks that agree with NFL API stats records
Train the 0 to 99 crop classifier
Roster join and name display

milestones.title: 3D virtual camera and film room
milestones.plain: Replay any play from any angle. Players get real 3D pose on key frames and the web film room lets you fly the camera behind the quarterback or above the safeties.
milestones.proof: A free-camera replay of one full drive.

stories.title: Film room: mobile layout pass
stories.note: Moved from M0 on close-out; rides with the film room.

stories.title: Film room edit mode: fix labels, identity, events and positions; review states and counters (built once real output exists)
stories.note: Designed 2026-09-13, blueprint 9.5, decision D-021.

stories.title: SAM 3D Body on keyframes
Spike: SAM 3D Body on 32 All-22 player crops (isolated and crowded, both angles, graded g/r/b) decides fitted bodies or posed capsules for GRD-59
stories.note: Done 2026-10-30 on the clear game (576p): fitted bodies for everyone. 27 player crops graded 15 good, 10 rough, 2 broken (5 sideline staff and officials left out); every isolated crop on both angles good or rough, smallest crops (43-59 px) fine; both broken crops are crowded line play on the sideline camera. 1.06 s per person on the M4 with the MHR body model on CPU (it needs float64), about 14.5 h per game at 6 keyframes. Untested: wide-shot players the detector misses at 576p.

Free camera replay of a drive

milestones.title: Play record API for clients
milestones.plain: Hand the play records to clients over the web. One JSON endpoint per play, filters over a whole game (every jet motion, every Cover 3, every 3rd and long), per-frame positions on request, and a bulk download of a whole game. Same database the chat uses.
milestones.proof: A client pulls a whole game as JSONL and filters plays by motion type and coverage over HTTP, with an API key.

stories.title: DuckDB view over the JSON records plus a hot-field table shared with the chat
FastAPI app: schema, games, plays with filters, one play, frame snapshot
Tracking endpoint: per-frame JSON or Parquet stream, by phase
Player endpoint: every play a player appears in with their per-play summary
Bulk export endpoints (JSONL, Parquet) with incremental pulls
API keys, versioned responses, stable error codes, client docs
Corrections endpoint and the flagged-review queue
Write side: create game from schedule, register film, check screen, analyze job, progress events
Film room: New game, drop film, check screen, one-button Analyze, per-play progress

milestones.title: Live pass
milestones.plain: Process plays as they happen from a single camera, seconds after the whistle, with fast models and honest confidence. Then, when the full two-angle film arrives, a post pass upgrades every play in place without touching anything a person corrected.
milestones.proof: A game processed from a single-angle recording played back in real time, each play landing within forty seconds of its whistle, and the record upgrading when the post pass runs afterward.

stories.title: Play boundaries from snap and whistle detection on a stream (no camera cuts)
Single-angle fusion mode with per-axis uncertainty
Incremental join to live official play-by-play (playStartTime), same count check
Two-pass record semantics: pass tag per field, post replaces live, corrections untouched, incremental API pulls
Latency budget measured and shown per play
Feasibility spike: broadcast feed (pans, zooms, replays, graphics)
